observation: Running the repository's own init commands inside a linked Git worktree (`git worktree add --detach`) reproduced two defects. `init doctor` reported `[WARN] Git: .git directory not found` for a valid checkout, and `init sync-githooks` wrote all six hook files and then printed `[WARN] sync githooks: no .git directory found; skipped core.hooksPath and commit.template`, so Git was never pointed at the hooks it had just installed. A third occurrence skipped the historical edit replay test in the same checkout. All three tested `is_dir($root . '/.git')`, but a linked worktree stores `.git` as a file. Two dogfood runners in the same tree already handled both shapes, so the assumption was inconsistent inside one repository.

evidence.summary: In a worktree created with `git worktree add --detach`, `php bin/agent-loop init doctor` printed `[WARN] Git: .git directory not found` and `php bin/agent-loop init sync-githooks` printed `[WARN] sync githooks: no .git directory found; skipped core.hooksPath and commit.template` while reporting `synced 6 hook file(s)`. After routing both through `GitWorkTree::detected()`, the same commands reported `[OK] Git: working tree detected` and `[OK] sync githooks: core.hooksPath=.githooks`.

Four assertions over a worktree the test creates itself. Reverting either production call site to `is_dir($root . '/.git')` fails the suite with two failures, so the regression falsifies the previous implementation rather than merely describing the new one.

hypothesis: Filesystem shape was treated as a repository contract. Because the failure is a silent WARN rather than an error, the hook integration can be inert in exactly the checkout layout agents use most.
validated_conclusion: Repository state is asked of Git, never inferred from the shape of `.git`. `GitWorkTree` owns the question; `NoGitDirectoryShapeAssumptionRule` fails production code that reintroduces the shape test. Tests stay out of the rule's scope because asserting that a linked worktree's `.git` really is a file is what makes the defect reproducible.
